PART I

Item 1. Business

MiniCorp designs, manufactures and markets widget accelerators and related services. The Company sells worldwide through its direct sales force and third-party resellers. MiniCorp was incorporated in Delaware in 1999 and is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. The Company operates a single reportable segment. Demand for widget accelerators is highly seasonal and concentrated in the fourth fiscal quarter. See Item 1A for a discussion of risks related to seasonality.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

The Company’s business is subject to a variety of risks. The market for widget accelerators is intensely competitive and characterized by rapid technological change. If the Company fails to introduce new products on a timely basis, revenue and gross margin would be materially adversely affected. The Company depends on a single contract manufacturer located in Asia; disruption at that facility, whether from natural disaster, public health crisis, or geopolitical conflict, would impair the Company’s ability to fulfill customer demand for an extended period.

The Company is exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates because a majority of revenue is denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar while most costs are dollar-denominated. A strengthening dollar has reduced and could continue to reduce reported revenue growth.

Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Net revenue increased 12% in fiscal 2025 compared to 2024, driven primarily by higher unit shipments of the WA-9 accelerator line. Gross margin expanded to 44.1% from 41.9%, reflecting favorable component pricing. Operating expenses grew 8%, slower than revenue, as headcount growth moderated.
